impact_scope.description: The existing public hasher.update! path gains automatic CPU-dependent dispatch to a new private SSE4.2 implementation; its caller-visible signature, input, configuration, and lifecycle remain unchanged.

evidence: In S0, pub func hasher.update!(x: roslice base.u8) already exists and accepts a byte slice.
H0 enables only AUX/BASE/JSON modules and exercises JSON decoders; it neither enables xxhash32 nor calls hasher.update!.
In S1, the identical public hasher.update!(x: roslice base.u8) surface remains the entry point.
The new choose up = [up_x86_sse42] dispatch and choosy private helper protocol are selected internally after the existing call; H0 still neither enables xxhash32 nor calls hasher.update!.

new_harness_obligation.description: No new H0 action is required to reach or control the change: callers still only supply the existing byte slice to hasher.update!, while CPU-path selection is automatic and the SIMD routine is private.
evidence: The public hasher.update! declaration retains the same parameter and call shape from S0 to S1.
The new CPU architecture choice is internal to hasher.update! and introduces no caller-supplied value, buffer, ordering transition, or explicit configuration.
H0's same-scope omission of the existing xxhash32 update API is unchanged.

reason: The principal unit is the existing public hasher.update! callable, not the newly added private SIMD sibling in isolation. H0 omits this same callable surface in both S0 and S1. S1 only adds an automatically selected internal implementation path, so caller-visible reachability and control obligations do not change.
